title: SQL Injection via mysqli/PDO String Interpolation
platform_conditions: PHP 7.4/8.x with PDO (MySQL driver emulates prepares by default: PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES on) or mysqli
security_mechanism: String interpolation composes the SQL text before the driver parses it, so a value containing a quote or SQL keyword is read as statement structure. PDO's MySQL driver additionally emulates prepared statements in the client by default, meaning the 'prepared' statement itself is assembled from the SQL string plus escaped values — historically exploitable when the escaping assumptions and the server sql_mode (e.g. NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES) disagree. Identifiers cannot be parameterized at all: ORDER BY, column and table names built by concatenation stay injection points even when values are bound.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters forming search values, sort keys, filter fields and pagination fragments passed into query text.
source_sink_clues.sink: $pdo->query / $pdo->exec / mysqli_query on interpolated strings; query builders receiving concatenated fragments for ORDER BY / LIMIT / column names

tracking_guards: Require prepare() + execute() with bound parameters, and for MySQL require PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false so prepares are real; require identifier parts to come from a fixed allowlist mapping client keys to column names; require LIMIT/OFFSET to pass through intval casting.
not_candidate_when: Values are bound through placeholders with server-side prepares, or the only interpolated parts are fixed allowlisted identifiers and integer-cast numbers, so no client text reaches the statement grammar.
public_references: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html
OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
